key_insight: A Monte Carlo simulation can convert published aggregate rare-cancer trial results into patient-level risk predictions, demonstrated in Ewing sarcoma.
clinical_relevance: This could help refine survivorship surveillance and future trial stratification, but it is not a substitute for validated individual-patient decision support.
method: Six-stage discrete-event Monte Carlo model combining genetic risk, serial biomarkers, ctDNA-MRD, and competing mortality risk
Calibrated using published Ewing sarcoma trial aggregates rather than individual patient data
Compared genotype-weighted vs equal-weight scoring and multi-timepoint vs single-timepoint risk stratification
evidence_signal: In validation against published data from more than 3,400 patients, the framework reported 3.2% mean absolute error across 23 efficacy endpoints and fit within confidence intervals for all 20 toxicity endpoints.
watch_item: The approach is built from published aggregate data and remains a hypothesis for transfer to other rare cancers until independently validated.
paper_title: WITHDRAWN: Multi-Timepoint Risk Stratification in Rare Cancers: A Computational Framework Validated against Published Ewing Sarcoma Trial Data
